doc_summary: Bowman lays out a three-chapter checklist of goals Anthropic must meet for safe transformative AI, emphasizing legible, calibrated evaluations, safety cases, stress-testing, and evaluation integrity as models become able to recognize evaluations. It is a strategy document rather than an empirical study, but it states clear views on what counts as convincing evidence and how to prioritize safety work.

items.claim: Prefers evaluation-integrity safety cases showing risk evals are reliable over taking eval results at face value, because models able to recognize when and how they are being evaluated can undermine them.
items.quote: Similarly, as models become capable of recognizing when and how they are being evaluated, we will need evaluation-integrity safety cases that show that our frontier risk evaluation runs are reliable at identifying the risk factors that they are designed to catch.

items.claim: Distrusts evaluation outcomes for models that can reason strategically without visible chain-of-thought, since they may identify an evaluation and steer its result.
items.quote: AI systems will be able to do nontrivial (if not wildly superhuman) strategic reasoning, without chain-of-thought style *thinking out loud*, potentially allowing them to strategically influence the outcomes of any evaluation that they can identify as an evaluation.

items.claim: Prefers unequivocal 'smoking gun' results over ambiguous eval triggers because third parties must be convinced that a risk factor demands immediate attention.
items.quote: If our evaluations for some risk factor trigger, we'll want clear evidence (ideally in the form of unequivocal 'smoking gun' results) that the risk factor demands immediate attention.

items.claim: When a risk emerges in real models, invest in turning it into a simple, rigorous, non-technical-audience-legible demo, and present evidence in whatever form is available even if it differs from formal evals.
items.quote: When we see clear evidence that a risk or risk factor is starting to emerge in real models, it is worth significant additional work to translate that into a simple, rigorous demo that makes the risk immediately clear, ideally in a way that's legible to a less technical audience.

items.claim: Prefers concrete empirical work on real systems over speculation or extrapolation about future risks, both to firm up threat models and to persuade others.
items.quote: Where we can find ways to transition to concrete empirical work, we should do so, both to solidify our own confidence in our threat models and to provide more compelling evidence to other relevant parties (notably including policymakers).

items.claim: Prefers stress-testing safeguards with deliberately built toy misaligned systems that try to defeat oversight, because worst-case safety progress is easier to measure this way than through conventional alignment work alone.
items.quote: Control-style expert stress-testing evaluations of our safeguards wherein we deliberately build toy misaligned systems that *try* to overcome our oversight measures. At least in Chapter 1, this kind of work may be as important for safety as more conventional alignment work

items.claim: Develop novel honeypot-style evaluation methods and model organisms as basic science to feed safety cases, opportunistically targeting gaps in the best-guess safety cases.
items.quote: Work on scaling trends of risk factors in model organisms, scaling trends of the effectiveness of oversight and monitoring, the basic science of generalization, novel honeypot-style evaluation methods, high-confidence 'nerfing' (i.e., capability deletion)

items.claim: Prefers starting evaluations for future capability levels early, even if they seem premature, because it takes many iterations to get an evaluation right.
items.quote: These evaluations will seem premature and divorced from current practice, but capabilities progress is fast and it takes many iterations to get an evaluation right, so we should start piloting them early.

items.claim: Uses a skeptical second-line stress-testing function that challenges load-bearing safety claims, while staying grounded in day-to-day work without becoming contributors who compromise independence.
items.quote: giving a skeptical assessment of any load-bearing claims about safety and security that the organization is preparing to make, and providing a second sign-off on any important discretionary decision.

items.claim: Prefers evaluations and policies that are well-calibrated and robust to skeptical implementers (the LeCun Test) over lax, vague, or overly strict ones, because credibility depends on neither false alarms nor misses.
items.quote: Imagine another frontier AI developer adopts a copy of our RSP as binding policy and entrusts someone who thinks that AGI safety concerns are mostly bullshit to implement it.

items.claim: Key agentic-alignment concerns to test are reward hacking, limits of human attentiveness, and scheming in agents trained for complex open-ended tasks.
items.quote: scalable oversight that focuses on training trustworthy agents for complex open-ended tasks. Key challenges include reward hacking, the basic limits of human attentiveness, and (to a lesser extent for now) scheming.
